query_text: Are there any academic fields that don't have enough people trying to teach?

messages.content: Are there any academic fields that don't have enough people trying to teach?

message.content:
Yes. Several academic teaching fields are described as having **shortages of people preparing to teach**, especially in **special education, English as a Second Language (ESL), math, science, and some higher-ed subject areas**.[2][6]

In K–12 teacher preparation, colleges have struggled to produce enough candidates overall, and one report notes that teacher prep programs have shrunk dramatically over time; only a small share of college freshmen say they plan to become teachers.[1] Another source says schools are “always looking” for special education, ESL, math, and science teachers, while elementary education and social studies tend to have more competition for jobs.[2]

At the postsecondary level, the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics projects about **114,000 openings for postsecondary teachers per year** over 2024–2034, mostly from replacement needs such as retirement, which indicates ongoing demand for people to teach in colleges and universities.[6]

If you mean **academic disciplines with especially few would-be teachers**, the clearest examples in the sources are **special education, ESL, math, and science**.[2]
